arabic_html:
ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُم بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ ۗ
أَلَا بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ ۞
translit:
Alladhīna āmanū wa taṭmaʾinnu qulūbuhum bi-dhikri-llāh.
Alā bi-dhikri-llāhi taṭmaʾinnu al-qulūb.
translation: Those who believe, and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God — truly, in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest.
translation_vo: Those who believe, and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God. Truly, in the remembrance of God, do hearts find rest.
explanation_html: The word is taṭmaʾinn — not a fleeting calm, but a settled stillness. Ibn Kathīr: the heart becomes tranquil when Allah is remembered, at rest knowing He is its protector. And Ibn ʿAbbās notes this remembrance includes the Qurʾān itself.
explanation_vo: The word here is tatma-inn. Not a fleeting calm, but a settled stillness. As Ibn Kathir explains, the heart becomes tranquil when Allah is remembered, at rest knowing He is its protector. And Ibn Abbas notes that this remembrance includes the Quran itself.
source: Source: Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr, 13:28 · with Tafsīr Ibn ʿAbbās
